a.raw: edmund said he was all right but he was feeling very sick
a.fixed: Edmund said he was all right, but he was feeling very sick.
a.why: Edmund is a name. A comma goes before but, because it joins two complete thoughts. Said and was are both past tense.

b.raw: lucy led the way and she found the faun's cave
b.fixed: Lucy led the way, and she found the Faun's cave.
b.why: Lucy is a name, and the Faun is used as his name. A comma goes before and. Led and found are both past tense.

cards.title: World Notes: Arctic Explorers
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: In Chapter 6, Lucy says they can pretend to be Arctic explorers.
The Arctic is the icy land and sea around the North Pole.
Explorers who went there wore thick fur clothes, a lot like the fur coats the children borrow from the wardrobe.

transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll form words, fix a passage in passes, and roll for beats.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 4 to 6 for your best evidence.

notes.wordParts: The root form means shape. uniform = one shape for everyone. transform = to change shape.
notes.grammar: Keep your verbs in the same time. If a story starts in the past (walked, ate), every verb stays in the past.
notes.spelling: Every beat in a word has one vowel sound. Count the sounds, not the letters: de-tail has two beats.
notes.wgrd: A choice leads to a consequence. Edmund chose to keep his secret, and it put his whole family in danger.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. The Witch spoke kindly and promised Edmund a crown, but Lucy said she was a terrible person. Spoke, promised and said all stay in the past. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the poem again. Then answer the question out loud.
mods.script: Here's Stevenson's poem again. He never says the word wind after the second line. So how do you know the rider is the wind? Read it out loud again, and answer out loud.

mods.todo: Tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means. Tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
mods.script: Quick! What does form mean? Shape! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Landform. A landform is a shape of the land, like a hill or a valley. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.

mods.todo: Choose one word. Write one sentence about Chapters 4 to 6.
mods.script: Here's how I'd use a word about the story. Superior. Edmund gave Lucy a superior look when he said they were only pretending. One word, one moment. Now choose one of your words and write your own sentence about Chapters 4 to 6.

mods.todo: Tap Check yourself. Tap every word that needs fixing. Then tap See the answers.
mods.script: Three passes, like an editor. Lucy said the queen was terrible and edmund feels sick. Pass one, capitals: Queen and Edmund. Pass two, verbs: feels slipped, so it becomes felt. Pass three, a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.

mods.todo: Tap Roll the dice. Split the word and say how you knew. Tap Check my answer.
mods.script: Here's my roll. Inquisitive. In, quis, i, tive. Four beats! How did I know? Four vowel sounds. Tap Roll the dice, split the word out loud, and say how you knew. Then tap Check my answer.

items.t: Edmund says, “You can't always believe what Fauns say.”
items.why: He says it to cover up that he has met the Queen.

items.t: Susan says she has a horrid feeling that Lu is right.
items.why: She says what she really thinks, even though she wants to go home.

items.t: The Professor says this is a very strange house, and even he knows very little about it.
items.why: He admits what he does not know.
